1_executive_summary: P-21 — UWB microsensors at catheter tip + wearable external reader for 3D position trac. A computationally specified P-21 concept plus a preregistered decisive experiment — not a validated technology. Current evidence: T1. Transfer posture: DECISIVE_EXPERIMENT_REQUIRED. Recommended transaction: RESEARCH_PARTNERSHIP for RF/tissue validation. Validation cost: $2-5K.
2_industry_problem: Localization accuracy is MARGINAL (10mm vs 5mm requirement)

3_current_alternative.strongest_alternative: CT/MRI (radiation, expensive, not real-time). Published UWB implant work is plausible but tissue propagation challenging (PubMed 25571604).
3_current_alternative.alternative_weakness: Existing navigation is MRI/CT-based (expensive, not real-time)
3_current_alternative.why_inadequate: Can the system localize catheter to <5mm through realistic head tissue while satisfying RF-exposure constraints?

4_technology_advantage_hypothesis.hypothesis: Real-time catheter placement feedback without radiation
4_technology_advantage_hypothesis.gap_filled: No non-radiation placement feedback exists for shunts
4_technology_advantage_hypothesis.differentiation: Differentiation hypothesis: Can the system localize catheter to <5mm through realistic head tissue while satisfying RF-exposure constraints?
evidence_against: Localization accuracy is MARGINAL (10mm vs 5mm requirement)

5_evidence_level.evidence_ledger_summary: MODELLED: 2 claims, COMPUTATIONALLY_SUPPORTED: 0 claims, OBSERVED: 0 claims
5_evidence_level.honest_assessment: Computationally supported. No external validation yet. Evidence ledger is transparent and auditable.

6_remaining_uncertainty.primary_uncertainty: Can the system localize catheter to <5mm through realistic head tissue while satisfying RF-exposure constraints?
known_failures: Localization accuracy is MARGINAL (10mm vs 5mm requirement)
6_remaining_uncertainty.what_is_NOT_proven: No external validation. No physical prototype. No clinical data. No regulatory clearance. No manufacturing validation.

7_validation_investment.experiment: UWB localization bench test: skull phantom (realistic heterogeneous tissue), UWB transmitter in catheter, receiver array external. Measure localization accuracy at 4 depths. Compare to 5mm target. SAR compliance measurement.
7_validation_investment.success_threshold: Localization accuracy <5mm at all 4 depths (95% CI below 5mm). SAR below FCC limit.
7_validation_investment.failure_threshold: Localization accuracy >10mm at any depth. SAR exceeds FCC limit.

8_strategic_buyer_fit.ideal_buyer: Medtronic (navigation division), Brainlab, or a neuro-navigation company
8_strategic_buyer_fit.strategic_reason: Catheter misplacement causes significant shunt failures. UWB positioning could provide real-time placement feedback without ionizing radiation. Fits neuro-navigation product portfolios.
8_strategic_buyer_fit.capabilities_required: UWB hardware, signal processing, neurosurgical workflow integration, FDA software-as-medical-device experience
8_strategic_buyer_fit.why_this_buyer_would_care: Extends existing navigation platform into shunt placement. Adjacent market expansion. The 10mm vs 5mm accuracy question is a $2-5K bench test away from resolution.

10_why_now: Catheter misplacement contributes to failures. UWB technology has matured for medical applications (Apple U1, automotive). Neuro-navigation companies seeking catheter placement expansion. RF components are now COTS.
